newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe cocoa stocks up, strong stg quietens trade.
newsitem.headline: Europe cocoa stocks up, strong stg quietens trade.

text.p: Cocoa arrivals into key western European ports mainly from the Ivory Coast continue apace but sterling's inexorable rise against European Continental currencies is keeping physical buyers at bay, trade sources said on Friday.
Fluctuations on the London terminal cocoa market in the past week, including a fall to a 18-month lows on Thursday, have failed to breathe life into physical trade.
"We were very disappointed in the level of business yesterday. Even though the price came off, Continental buyers saw hardly any decrease," a continental-based trader commented.
"The British currency is not helping at all."
Cocoa futures rebounded on Friday, the benchmark May contract coming back up to around 890 stg a tonne.

Traders noted physical differentials were little changed, with Ivorian beans nearby trading 20/25 stg under the terminal market, March at 15/20 stg under and April 25 stg under. New crop was quoted around 10/15 stg under. Ghanaian cocoa was about level the terminal and Cameroon beans were slightly below that.
They added the cocoa butter ratio was static at about 2.64 for this year, 2.62 for next, but demand was slack for products.
The market's general weakness has been linked to the high availablity of cocoa and the latest figures from warehousing firm SGS reveal that stocks in Europe are continuing to swell.

SGS said at the end of January/early February, cocoa beans stored in Amsterdam totalled 516,000 tonnes, up almost 50,000 tonnes from a month earlier. In Hamburg, inventories were up more than 10,000 tonnes to 122,000.
"There's a lot of cocoa arriving, and a lot of it is arriving in bulk," said one trade source.
Bulk cocoa shipments -- in contrast to bagged imports -- are an increasingly prominent feature of the Amsterdam cocoa trade.
